request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Pallas by TxPipe maintenance and enhancement for Year 2, including Intersect administration fee.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 420,000 ADA plus a 105,000 ADA contingency reserve and a 15,750 ADA Intersect administration fee, totaling 540,750 ADA.

Pallas is a collection of Rust crates re-implementing core Ouroboros and Cardano primitives including CBOR encoding, cryptographic operations, mini-protocol networking, multi-era ledger traversal, transaction building, and address handling.
Pallas serves as shared infrastructure for projects including Aiken, Dolos, Lucid, Oura, Mithril, Amaru, UTxO-RPC, and others.
The proposal states Pallas has over 649 pull requests, 199 stars, 91 forks, 60 contributors, and 214,446 crates.io downloads, with links to GitHub and crates.io.
The maintainer scope covers essential maintenance, community support, and AI-friendly documentation and integration resources.
The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and was advanced for on-chain Treasury Withdrawal submission.
The proposal states the requested amount does not breach the 350M Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the time of submission.
Audit, administrative oversight, reporting obligations, and milestone-based disbursement controls are described as being provided through Intersect and technically capable third parties.
TxPipe is stated to have received funding through 30 Project Catalyst proposals across Funds 9 through 14, with 26 delivered and 4 under development and on schedule.

Intersect will administer the withdrawn funds through Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts using a TRSC and PSSC with specified addresses, multisignature role thresholds, external oversight entities, and a public dashboard.

summary: The document requests 540,750 ADA for a 12-month Pallas maintenance program by TxPipe, administered by Intersect through treasury smart contracts with stated oversight, milestones, and community audit mechanisms.
